claims.statement: Constable Fred Lenz failed on April 21, 1903 to replevin the driving horse claimed by Tillie Hartgrove, Tom Allen's former housekeeper.
claims.excerpt: in replevining the driving horse claimed by Miss Tillie Hartgrove, former housekeeper for Tom Allen

claims.statement: The horse was in the possession of William W. Heapes in St. Louis County.
claims.excerpt: The horse is in possession of William W. Ileapes in St. Louis County.

claims.statement: Tillie Hartgrove claims the horse was a gift to her from Allen.
claims.excerpt: Mrs. Hartgrove. who says he was a gift to her

claims.statement: G. A. Strode, as administrator of Allen's estate, also claimed the horse.
claims.excerpt: of the estate of Tom Allen; by Heapes, for a feed bill.

claims.statement: William W. Heapes would hold the horse until a feed bill of some $17 was settled.
claims.excerpt: that he would hold on to the steed until a feed bill of some $17 was settied.

claims.statement: Constable Fred Lenz also claimed the horse under an execution writ.
claims.excerpt: Heapes, for a feed bill. and by Lenz, with an execution writ.

notes: Lists the competing claims to the horse (Hartgrove, Strode, Heapes, Lenz). Heapes's name is OCR 'Ileapes' in the text.
